title: The firms that are paid to lobby
question: Which firms and in-house teams take in the money, and how concentrated is the business?
finding: 329 firms, sole practitioners and in-house teams reported payments; 88 of them sell lobbying to three or more outside clients and took 96.4% of the total. Five names account for 68.2%: Lighthouse Public Affairs ($33.1 million), HMS Associates ($24.7 million), Noyola Piccini Group ($22.1 million), New Deal Advisers ($19.9 million), Platinum Advisors ($18.5 million).
how: Payments are summed by the firm named on each report (or by the lobbyist’s own name where no firm is given). A longer firm name that begins with a shorter one and shares a lobbyist is treated as the same firm. A firm counts as selling lobbying when it reports three or more clients other than itself and most of its contacts and payments are for them.
limits: Lobbying is registered, and so is giving by a lobbyist’s clients and colleagues. A firm that changed its name appears once under each name unless the names share their opening words and a lobbyist. Law firms report only the part of their fees they treat as lobbying, so a law firm with many clients can show small sums. “City paid the firm” is a name match against the payment ledger and can catch a different business with the same name.
